title: "Concept map"
description: "The quantities answer different questions; this page keeps them separate."
---

## One projection, several geometries

| Object | Question | Governing quantity | Isotropic value |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Distance value | How much centered distance variance is recoverable? | `alpha_m(Sigma)` | `m/d` |
| Arbitrary distance feature | Can any nonlinear decoder do better? | squared HGR ceiling | `m/d` |
| Pairwise order | Does candidate A remain closer than B? | Beta–arcsine law | exact finite `m,d` |
| Full ranking | How many pairwise orders agree? | expected Kendall tau | `2 p_{m,d} - 1` |
| Nearest of `q` | Does the argmin agree? | plurality kernel `p_q` | score-limit law |
| Mean / scale | How much local Fisher information remains? | Haar average | `m/d` |
| Diffuse covariance shape | How much scale-adjusted shape information remains? | Haar average | `(m-1)(m+2)/((d-1)(d+2))` |

## Baseline versus fluctuation

For two independent Gaussian observations,

$$
\mathbb E D=2\operatorname{tr}\Sigma,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(D)=8\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2).
$$

The mean is the large common baseline. Rankings use the much smaller centered
fluctuations. Their relative scale is controlled by

$$r_2(\Sigma)=\frac{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma)^2}{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)}.$$

## Decoder-free does not mean estimator performance

HGR maximal correlation takes the best correlation over *all* square-integrable
transformations on both sides. It is an impossibility ceiling: no decoder can
beat it. A concrete estimator may perform strictly worse.

## Known maps: rank, spread, precision

A known noiseless map has three distinct summaries:

- **Rank** governs optimal inference after reversible row whitening.
- **Spectral spread** governs an unwhitened norm estimate `||Tx||²`.
- **Small singular values** govern stability when additive noise is present.

Conflating these summaries is the quickest route to a misleading claim.
